bacteriophage: A single panoramic scientific illustration centers on a geometric bacteriophage, its icosahedral protein head packed with a tiny coiled genome, landing like a lunar module on one specific rod-shaped bacterium while ignoring neighboring bacterial species of different shapes and colors; the phage’s tail injects its genetic instructions as a glowing stream, after which the bacterium swells and ruptures, releasing a swarm of identical new phages. Human cells and tissues in the same frame remain completely untouched and healthy, emphasizing that the virus never infects people. In the surrounding laboratory-and-clinic setting, a computer screen displays an AI system assembling and rewriting those same minuscule genomes into novel sequences, while a physician administers the resulting custom phages to a patient whose infection has already shrugged off conventional antibiotic pills; a few surviving bacteria display mutated surface proteins that confer resistance, visually arguing why researchers must keep designing fresh phages rather than relying solely on those found in nature, and a discreet world map in the corner marks the countries already using this therapy.
genome-language-model: A panoramic laboratory-and-compute scene shows thousands of uncoiled DNA helices rendered as four-letter A-C-G-T text strings streaming from stacked genome libraries into a glowing neural-network “chatbot” labeled Evo1/Evo2; the model emits statistically similar but novel sequences while a thought-bubble robot merely predicts letter co-occurrence without biological insight. Those synthetic strings become physical DNA pipetted into living cells under a microscope that splits into a functional virus versus an inert molecule, proving wet-lab testing is required. Surrounding icons of other genome types, locked data vaults, access-control gates, and DNA-order screening machines sit beside arguing scientists, visually encoding the open questions of training data, users, and safeguards.
phage-therapy: A richly detailed scientific illustration centers on a hospital patient receiving an injection against a stubborn infection, with a large magnified circular inset revealing lunar-lander-shaped bacteriophages precisely attaching to and bursting only the disease-causing bacteria while neighboring beneficial microbes remain unharmed, set against a dimmer background panel of antibiotics indiscriminately wiping out the entire microbiome; arrows trace bacteria rapidly mutating into resistant forms, while a glowing AI workstation in the foreground generates an entirely novel, fully functional phage genome as a complete synthetic DNA helix unlike any collected from nature, materializing into custom phages that launch to outpace adaptation, with faded historical medical manuscripts in one corner reminding that the therapy itself is old even as the computer-written complete genomes mark what is new.
